inventory.source_text: n,N range over Nat, E=Euclidean R^(n+1), S=unit sphere, M={x:Fin N->S}. N=0 is allowed: the product is a point, all coordinate sums are empty and the identities are zero=zero. n=0 is also allowed: S is the two-point zero-dimensional sphere. There is no positive-dimension restriction hidden in a truncated dimension subtraction.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: tau=(Lebesgue measure on E).toSphere, the polar measure on S. Its total mass is finite and strictly positive because dim(E)=n+1>0. sigma=tau(S)^(-1) tau, with inverse in the nonnegative extended reals and scalar multiplication of measures. The product measure is the finite measure product over i in Fin N. It is an actual probability measure; no arbitrary measure sigma is supplied.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: For any sphere function h with codomain R or E, define its canonical radial extension h^r on E by h^r(z)=h(z/||z||) when z!=0 and h^r(0)=0. The value at zero is merely a total-function convention. Every derivative defining a sphere operator is taken at a unit vector inside the open nonzero region. No differentiability or continuity at zero is required or implied.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: For x in S, P_x is the actual orthogonal projection onto x-perp: P_x v=v-<v,x>x. Define grad_S h(x)=P_x grad_E(h^r)(x). For W:S->E define div_S W(x)=div_E(W^r)(x), where div_E is the coordinate trace of the Frechet derivative. Under C1 regularity the first operator is the ordinary intrinsic gradient; the second is the ordinary intrinsic divergence when W is tangent; proving their tangent-differential/trace identification is part of the required bridge, not a new assumption.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: For x in M, write x[i<-y] for configuration x with coordinate i replaced by y. Define grad_i f(x)=grad_S(y->f(x[i<-y]))(x_i), and div_M V(x)=sum_i div_S(y->V_i(x[i<-y]))(x_i). Pairings are sum_i<grad_i f(x),V_i(x)> with no factor 1/N. This is the product Riemannian operator and normalization.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: Intrinsically Ck means Ck in the ordinary stereographic charts on S and finite product charts on M. The vector field components are Ck maps from M to the ambient Euclidean E, with pointwise tangency. No globally Ck ambient extension is supplied; canonical radial regularity away from the zero coordinates must be derived from these intrinsic hypotheses.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: Use the smooth radial normalization on E minus {0}, the stereographic sphere charts and product charts to derive C1 or C2 regularity of the canonical extension wherever every coordinate is nonzero. Establish extension agreement on S, tangent differentiation, the radial derivative zero identity, and identification with the induced metric operators. The artificial zero value at the origin is never used as a differentiability premise.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: Multiply the radial extension of a tangent field by a smooth scalar radial cutoff supported in a positive annulus. This produces a globally C1 compactly supported ambient field as an internal construction. Apply the existing whole-space zero-divergence producer, and the existing Haar-to-sphere polar decomposition. Tangency kills the derivative of the radial cutoff. The remaining radial factor is integral chi(r)/r * r^n dr; choose it nonzero and cancel it. No new proof of the ambient divergence theorem or ball-flux theorem is needed.
inventory.author_coverage_claim: represented; independent source/reader validation is separate

inventory.source_text: Derive the actual tangent product rule div_S(fW)=<grad_S f,W>+f div_S W using the canonical radial derivatives and existing orthogonal-projection identities. Apply P2 to fW. Compactness and intrinsic regularity derive integrability; no IBP identity is assumed.

inventory.source_text: Scale both sides by the explicit reciprocal polar surface mass, identify sigma exactly, and apply single-sphere identities to coordinate sections. Joint intrinsic C1 regularity gives continuous section derivatives and integrability on the compact product. Finite-product Fubini and finite summation yield F1-F2 with no 1/N factor, including the empty product.
